absent: Target selection oracle, active list summary, sorting and register population details
Physical deactivation, completion notification, resampling and reference counting behavior
Control, status and trap bit layouts and maintenance interrupt generation rules
Third generation single register fold and second generation control configuration
Fifth generation private visibility, identifier mapping and enable synchronization
Nested state detection, virtual register access and virtual processing element commit
Lock ordering, allocation lifetime and error handling for descriptor lookup

findings.text: Top level guest entry preparation distinguishes nested execution from normal execution. In nested mode it records a virtual hypervisor interrupt request when any virtual interrupt is pending and only enables the virtual interface before returning. In normal mode with nesting support it refreshes maintenance state, then flushes software list state to hardware images, restores hardware state when kernel access is allowed, and commits direct interrupt state when both software and hardware support are present.

This lane provides virtual interface management helpers for folding processor list or private state, saving and restoring processor interface images, flushing software state to hardware images, flushing nested control, and committing direct interrupt virtual processing element state across second, third and fifth generation interfaces.

Flush, fold, save and restore each dispatch on interrupt controller generation. Fifth generation uses dedicated private interrupt helpers and returns early. Older generations select between second and third generation helpers based on a global type flag or branch indicator. Kernel access to the interface is available for memory mapped control or when virtualization host extensions are present.

List register values derive from the software interrupt descriptor starting from its virtual identifier. Active state adds an active encoding and for gates needing multiple registers suppresses pending and requests maintenance on completion. Hardware backed interrupts without resampling add a hardware encoding plus physical identifier and never combine pending with active. Level configured software interrupts add maintenance on completion and also suppress pending while active. Otherwise pending state adds a pending encoding. Group and priority are always encoded, with second generation keeping only upper priority bits.

Software generated interrupts carry a source set and an active source identifier. When building a register value for a pending gate the lowest set source becomes the encoded source, and any additional set sources cause a maintenance request. Second generation compatibility handling applies when the virtual model selects second generation, covering both active source and pending source encodings.

The number of registers required by a descriptor is one when pending or active, except for software gates with a non empty source set where it equals the population count of sources plus one if active. A descriptor needing more than one register is treated as a multi source gate.

Folding a second generation register extracts virtual identifier and source index, notifies completion for level shared peripherals that signal maintenance without hardware involvement, then under the descriptor lock refreshes active state from the register while noting deactivation, records source for active gates, preserves pending as latched state only for edge configuration while merging gate sources, clears latched state for level configuration lacking any state, invokes resampling handling with deactivation and pending indications, and marks the descriptor as no longer resident.

Bulk folding covers each used register in order and resets the used count, and when a last resident marker exists walks the remainder of the active list. While a hardware completion count remains, each subsequent descriptor that still targets the same processor and remains active is re encoded without active state, physically deactivated when hardware backed, folded back as if the processor had done so, and consumes one count. The walk assumes priority ordered deactivation in reverse activation order after priority drop.

Fifth generation private state is exchanged through host active and pending bitmaps. On exit the active bitmap is copied into each visible descriptor active flag and the pending bitmap is merged by logical alternative into latched state for edge configuration only, then the exit active bitmap becomes the next entry shadow. On entry a fresh pending bitmap is built from current pending evaluation while clearing edge latched state, then stored as the host pending shadow for later hardware programming and merging of arrivals during execution.

Saving preserves control state and list contents while disabling the control register. Live list contents are determined with an empty status word where empty slots keep stored value with state cleared, occupied slots are read back from hardware, and hardware slots are then cleared. Completion count merging occurs only when maintenance reporting was enabled. Restoring programs the control register combined with trap requirements then programs each used slot. Ordering barriers surround the transfer when any slot is used or host extensions are absent and snooping is disabled. Nested flush only rewrites the control register with trap requirements.

Fifth generation control save captures virtual machine control and interrupt status. Private save captures active, pending and lower priority banks into host and interface shadows then disables direct injection. Private restore re enables injection from the shadow, restores active and enable banks, restores pending only for entries not under direct injection by masking host pending with the injection mask, restores lower priority banks, and clears all upper bank control, active, enable, pending and priority state. Full save and restore pair control and private helpers with a synchronization barrier.

Flushing builds a summary of the active list, sorts by priority when some entries cannot fit, clears the last resident marker, then walks the list and populates consecutive registers only for entries still targeting the current processor. When capacity is reached a reference is held on the boundary entry as the marker and the walk stops. Remaining slots are cleared and the used count plus control configuration are recorded in the generation specific interface area.

Active list mutation during flush requires holding the per processor active list lock with interrupts disabled, asserted by the implementation. Each descriptor examined or updated during flush, fold or private exchange is protected by its own interrupt lock, using interrupt saving form for fifth generation private paths. Bulk fold and top level flush require disabled interrupts. Lookup and boundary marker references are balanced with release.

A descriptor cycles between software pending, resident in a register, and active states. Entry transition marks residency and for edge private state clears software latch after sampling. Exit transition clears residency, refreshes active from hardware, merges or clears latch according to trigger type, and for gates merges sources. Extra hardware completion indications advance additional active tail entries through deactivation without resident registers. Direct virtual processing element commit occurs once until invalidated.

Each processor keeps generation specific interface shadows holding used count, register image array, control and machine control images and trap related flags, plus for fifth generation private active, enable, injection and priority shadows and host exit active and pending bitmaps. Global state holds type selection, control base addresses and register capacity. Virtual processing element state holds a readiness flag.

Building a register value while the descriptor is already marked resident triggers a warning. Building a pending gate value with an empty source set warns with rate limiting and yields a zero value that carries no valid state. Edge pending merges must use logical alternative on both exit and entry paths to avoid losing concurrent arrivals. Status spanning more than one word requires reading an extended status word. Null control base causes save and restore to return without touching hardware.

Fifth generation private interrupt count is sixty four with eight lower priority banks preserved and eight upper banks cleared, enforced by a compile time check. Second generation register priority keeps five bits derived from upper bits of software priority.
